title: NASA-UAP-D015, Astronaut Scientific Debriefings, 1962-1963
doc_notes: This document contains transcripts and memoranda regarding astronaut observations of luminous phenomena and atmospheric layers during the Mercury program, specifically focusing on the 'Glenn effect' and scientific experiments conducted by astronauts. / This document is a transcript of a NASA scientific debriefing with astronaut Walter Schirra regarding his October 1962 orbital flight, focusing on atmospheric phenomena and visual observations.

incidents.summary: Astronaut John Glenn reported seeing thousands of luminous particles traveling with the Friendship-7 spacecraft at sunrise.
behavior: moving at same speed and direction
incidents.explanation: Particles associated with the spacecraft or booster, likely snowflakes from life-support steam or dust/insulation.
incidents.quote: thousands of luminous particles apparently travelling with the spacecraft

incidents.summary: Astronaut John Glenn observed a luminous band 6-8 degrees above the horizon with a haze layer.
incidents.explanation: Likely airglow or MIE scattering from dust.
incidents.quote: band six to eight degrees above the horizon

incidents.summary: Astronaut Scott Carpenter observed a luminous band around the horizon using an airglow filter.
incidents.explanation: Identified as the 5577 Angstrom airglow layer.
incidents.quote: luminous band visible around the horizon

incidents.summary: Astronaut Gordon Cooper observed a flashing light beacon ejected from the spacecraft.
incidents.quote: The light is flashing, now. It is the light.

incidents.summary: Astronaut Gordon Cooper observed luminous particles streaming from the spacecraft after thruster firing.
incidents.quote: tremendous streams of luminous particles of fireflies

incidents.summary: Astronaut Schirra observed a luminous brownish smog-like layer or belt while in orbit over the Indian Ocean/Africa region.
incidents.explanation: The phenomenon was discussed as a potential high-altitude smog or atmospheric layer, possibly related to magnetic anomalies or nitrogen effects, though Schirra expressed skepticism about nitrogen outgassing.
incidents.quote: It was definitely toward the brown smog thing. Sort of Brownish gray - rather it wasn't black or white.
